content: Hūṃ! Homage to the Swift-Acting Avalokiteśvara!With anklets on his feet, he tramples upon Vināyaka.The Great Black One wears a tiger-skin lower garment,And is fully adorned with ornaments of snakes.His right hand holds a blazing curved knife and a rosary,And with the last, he fiercely rattles a ḍamaru.His left hands hold a skull-cup and a trident,And likewise, he grasps a lasso with which he binds.His wrathful mouth bares its fangs,His three eyes are fierce, and his hair blazes upward.His forehead is well-anointed with sindūra,And his crown is firmly sealed by the King Akṣobhya.He wears a necklace of fifty blood-dripping human heads,And his head is adorned with five dry jeweled skulls.Having come forth from the tree to accept this torma,To the glorious Six-Armed One, I prostrate and offer praise.Protect the solemn teachings of the Buddha,Exalt the majestic status of the Three Jewels,And for us—master, disciples, and retinue—May all adverse conditions and obstacles be pacified,And please swiftly bestow the siddhis we desire.Hūṃ, to the Guru and Protector, inseparable,With devotion I take refuge.May I, for the sake of all sentient beings,Clear away their afflictions without exception.To the Protector and Guru, inseparable,With devotion I take refuge.May I, for the sake of all sentient beings,Clear away their obstacles without exception. (Recite three times.)To the White Protector, the Wish-Fulfilling Jewel,With devotion I take refuge.May I, for the sake of all sentient beings,Clear away their poverty without exception.Through this virtue, throughout all my successive lives,May I uphold the Victors' sacred Dharma without exception,And by dispelling all adverse conditions and fulfilling all favorable ones,May the Guru and Protector accomplish this without delay.
